subject: Flight plan to acceptance: success anchors & exit gates
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@healthfin.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Flight plan to acceptance: success anchors & exit gates

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise flight plan that lays out success anchors, concrete exit gates, and the acceptance tests we’ll run during the evaluation. The goal is to make sign-off objective and unblock procurement/technical review in the same two-week window.

High-level asks from HealthFin:
- 2-week evaluation window starting Nov 30 (you indicated that works)
- Sandbox dataset (PII-masked) and a test API key for traffic simulation
- Procurement/Legal checklist completed by Dec 10

Proposed success anchors (what "good" looks like):
1) Functional: end-to-end feature parity for claims parsing + templated responses for 80% of top 20 intents (sample set attached).
2) Performance: p95 latency < 350 ms for 32-token responses at baseline load (see perf-stub).
3) Reliability: <1% application-level error rate and graceful fallback to smaller model on overload.
4) Quality: precision@top1 >= 88% for the labeled intent test suite.

Exit gates (hard stops we will not pass without sign-off):
- Any security blocker flagged by your security questionnaire that requires architecture changes.
- Data residency/handling constraints that cannot be met in the Dedicated configuration.
- Regression in any of the three production-mirroring tests: throughput, latency, and intent precision.

Acceptance tests (deliverables we will hand you):
- Instrumented smoke suite (automation + runbook) to verify functional flows.
- Perf report: steady-state throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, and cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Concordance report: labeling of 500 sample items against reference set and confusion matrix.

Attachments: HF-MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), acceptance-tests-v0.3.md (tests & pass criteria), perf-runbook-stub.pdf (ops checklist).

Next steps: can you confirm the evaluation start date and share the sandbox dataset link? If Dec 10 procurement cutover is tight we can move sign-off windows around but want to lock the objective metrics now.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@healthfin.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthfin.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Flight plan to acceptance: success anchors & exit gates

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we commit to the Nov 30 start: 
1) Performance: our baseline production latency target is p95 < 300 ms for single-region traffic. Is the 350 ms target above optimistic for the hosted sandbox or intentionally relaxed?
2) Data: we'll provide a PII-masked subset (~10k records). Can you confirm you have tooling to validate masking and that logs will not contain PII?
3) Acceptance tests: will the concordance set include examples of long-form claim narratives? Our edge cases are often 400–800 tokens.

Procurement loop: we (procurement@healthfin.io) will circulate the SOW draft this week. Legal will want the fallback/failover notes in the MAP for SLAs. Amit (cc’d on future messages) is our outside counsel and will handle redlines.

If you can answer the three bullets above we’ll confirm the Nov 30 start by EOD Friday Nov 12.

— Erin
Head of Product, HealthFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@healthfin.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Flight plan to acceptance: success anchors & exit gates

Thanks Erin — quick notes from Customer Success to ensure the acceptance tests are runnable and auditable: 

- Mask validation: we’ll run a PII-scan on the sandbox and produce a short report (hashing, token patterns) to confirm no raw PII reaches logs. We’ll also set log redaction at the edge.
- Long-form narratives: concordance will include a 150-long and 10 long-form (400–800 token) subset specifically targeted at your edge cases. Those long-form cases are run with a fixed max-seq length and measured separately in the perf report.
- Canary plan: we’ll do a 2-step canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> full) with go/no-go checks at each step based on error rate and latency deltas.

Suggested timeline (compressed):
- Nov 30: eval start, baseline smoke run, initial perf sweep
- Dec 2: feature demo and walk-through of concordance results
- Dec 6: canary ramp + procurement/contract decision checkpoint
- Dec 10: target sign-off / exec summary delivered

We’ll push an updated MAP with these checkpoints into the shared spreadsheet and attach the smoke script examples.

— Marissa
Sr Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@healthfin.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Flight plan to acceptance: success anchors & exit gates

Erin — Jordan —

Technical confirmation from solutions engineering: the acceptance test matrix we will run in the sandbox looks like this (summary):

- Functional smoke: 250 cases, pass threshold 95% (automated)
- Concordance: 500 labeled items -> precision@top1 >= 88% (must hit both overall and on the 10 long-form samples)
- Perf sweep:
  * Single-connection baseline: p50/p95/p99: < 120 ms / < 240 ms / < 480 ms (local infra)
  * Simulated burst (50 concurrent sessions, 2 minute window): sustained p95 < 350 ms
  * Throughput: verified at 200 rps sustained for 10 minutes without qps throttling
- Cost delta test: run 1k sample tokens across baseline and quantized model and report $/1k tokens estimate.

Notes: the p95 300 ms target Erin mentioned is achievable on Dedicated pools with tuned batching; for hosted/sandbox we conservatively provision to 350 ms to account for variability. If HealthFin needs stricter SLA we can pin a Dedicated pool in the trial window (adds procurement steps).

Action items for HealthFin to unblock tests:
- Provide masked dataset link (S3 or secure Drive) + test account with 200 sample synthetic API keys by Nov 24.
- Confirm whether you want a Dedicated trial (if yes, we’ll include simple cost estimate and provisioning runbook).

I’ve attached a perf-runbook-stub.pdf and a small script snippet in the MAP spreadsheet.

— Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@healthfin.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@healthfin.io>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Flight plan to acceptance: success anchors & exit gates

Erin / team —

Thanks — this is great alignment. Finalizing the MAP now and attaching HF-MAP-v1.xlsx with the timeline and owner columns filled in. Key commitments from Redwood:
- Instrumented smoke suite ready by Nov 30 AM
- Perf sweep and concordance report by Dec 2 EOD
- Canary ramp playbook (if chosen) by Dec 4
- Executive sign-off package and cost estimate by Dec 10

Please confirm: 1) dataset link and 2) whether you want us to include a Dedicated trial quote (we can surface cost impact and procurement checklist). If we get dataset + Dedicated flag by Nov 24 we can keep the timeline above.

If all good, I’ll drop a short DocuSign MPA link into the spreadsheet for quick signature — this will lock the evaluation start and give both teams a neutral go/no-go rhythm.

Thanks — Jordan
